p.src: The story goes that Li Kui said, “Brother, tell me those three conditions.” Song Jiang said, “You are going to Yishui County in Yizhou to bring your mother here. First, go straight home and do not drink any wine. Second, with your fiery temper, who would be willing to accompany you? You must quietly fetch your mother and come straight back. Third, do not take those two broad axes of yours. Be cautious on the road, and return as swiftly as you can.” Li Kui said, “Why should I not obey those three conditions? Rest easy, brother. I shall leave today without another moment’s delay.” Li Kui promptly bound up his clothes for travel. Wearing only a sword at his waist and carrying a long-handled broadsword, he took a large ingot of silver and three or five smaller pieces, drank several cups of wine, made a deep salute, bade everyone farewell, and descended the mountain, passing beyond Golden Sands Beach.

p.src: After Chao Gai, Song Jiang, and the other chiefs had seen him off, they returned to the stronghold and took their seats in the Hall of Righteous Assembly. Still uneasy, Song Jiang said to the others, “Brother Li Kui is certain to meet with trouble on this journey. Do any of you brothers come from his home district? Such a man could go there and learn what news there is of him.” Du Qian said, “Only Zhu Gui is a native of Yishui County in Yizhou; he comes from the same district.” Hearing this, Song Jiang said, “I had forgotten. When we gathered at White Dragon Temple the other day, Li Kui himself recognized Zhu Gui as a fellow countryman.” Song Jiang immediately sent someone to summon Zhu Gui. A young bandit hurried down the mountain with the message, went directly to the tavern, and brought Zhu Gui back. Song Jiang said, “Brother Li Kui has now gone to his native village to bring his aged mother here. Because he behaves badly in his cups, I would not send anyone with him, yet I truly fear that trouble may befall him on the road. Now that I know you are from his district, go there and learn what you can of him.” Zhu Gui replied, “I am from Yishui County in Yizhou. I have a younger brother named Zhu Fu who keeps a tavern outside the western gate of the county town. Li Kui’s family lives at Dong’s Inn in Baizhang Village in that same county. He has an elder brother named Li Da, who hires himself out as a permanent farmhand. Li Kui was fierce and unruly from childhood. After killing a man, he fled into the world of wanderers and has never once returned home. There is no harm in sending me there now to inquire after him, though I fear there will be no one to mind my tavern. It has also been a long time since I went home, so I should like to take the opportunity to visit my brother.” Song Jiang said, “Do not worry about the tavern. I shall have Hou Jian and Shi Yong manage it for you for a while.” Having received these instructions, Zhu Gui took leave of all the chiefs and descended the mountain. He went to the tavern, packed his bundle, handed the establishment over to Shi Yong and Hou Jian, and set off for Yizhou.

p.src: Now Li Kui, traveling alone after leaving Liangshan Marsh, followed the road until he reached the borders of Yishui County. On the way Li Kui truly drank no wine, and so caused no trouble; there is nothing further to relate of the journey. When he reached the western gate of Yishui County, he saw a crowd gathered around a proclamation. Li Kui stood among them and heard someone read aloud, “First among the principal rebels is Song Jiang, a native of Yuncheng County; second among the accomplices is Dai Zong, formerly chief gaoler of the two prisons of Jiangzhou; third among the accomplices is Li Kui, a native of Yishui County in Yizhou.” Hearing this from the rear of the crowd, Li Kui was just about to wave his arms and make a commotion, with no notion what to do, when a man suddenly rushed forward, seized him around the waist, and cried, “Brother Zhang, what are you doing here?” Li Kui twisted around to look and recognized Zhu Gui, the “Dry-Land Crocodile.” Li Kui asked, “How did you come to be here too?” Zhu Gui said, “Just follow me, and we shall talk.”

p.src: Together they went to a tavern in a village near the western gate, walked straight to a quiet room at the back, and sat down. Pointing at Li Kui, Zhu Gui said, “You are astonishingly bold! That proclamation plainly offers ten thousand strings of cash for the capture of Song Jiang, five thousand for Dai Zong, and three thousand for Li Kui. How could you stand there reading it? What would you have done if some sharp-eyed, quick-handed fellow had seized you and delivered you to the authorities? Brother Song Gongming feared you would cause trouble and therefore would not let anyone accompany you. Still fearing that you might do something outrageous here, he afterward sent me expressly to hasten after you and learn what had become of you. I descended the mountain a day later than you, yet arrived here a day before you. How is it that you have only reached this place today?” Li Kui said, “It was because our brother ordered me not to drink wine, and that made me travel more slowly along the road. How do you know this tavern? You are from this region, but where does your family live?” Zhu Gui said, “This tavern belongs to my younger brother Zhu Fu. I was born in this region. Later I went abroad as a merchant, lost my capital, and so joined the outlaws at Liangshan Marsh. This is the first time I have returned.” He then called his younger brother Zhu Fu, and introduced him to Li Kui. Zhu Fu set out wine to entertain Li Kui. Li Kui said, “Our brother ordered me not to drink, but now that I have reached my home district, what damned harm can there be in drinking a couple of bowls?” Zhu Gui dared not restrain him and let him drink as he pleased.

p.src: That night Li Kui drank until the fourth watch. Some food was prepared, and after eating it, he set out for the village in the fifth watch, beneath fading stars and a waning moon, as the bright glow of dawn spread across the sky. Zhu Gui instructed him, “Do not take the narrow path. Turn by the great hackberry tree, enter the eastern highway, and follow it straight to Baizhang Village; there you will come to Dong’s Inn. Fetch your mother quickly, and let us return early to the mountain stronghold together.” Li Kui said, “Is not the narrow path nearer? Who has the patience to follow the highway?” Zhu Gui said, “There are many tigers on the narrow path, as well as highwaymen who seize travelers’ bundles whenever they see the chance.” Li Kui replied, “What the devil have I to fear?” Putting on his felt cap, he took up his long-handled broadsword, fastened his sword at his waist, bade Zhu Gui and Zhu Fu farewell, and went out the door toward Baizhang Village.

p.src: As he walked on, he saw ahead a tangled grove of some fifty large trees. It was early autumn, and the leaves were turning red. When Li Kui reached the edge of the grove, a burly man suddenly stepped out and shouted, “If you know what is good for you, leave a toll for me, or I’ll take your bundle too!” Li Kui looked him over. He wore a red silk knotted headscarf and a coarse padded jacket, held two broad axes in his hands, and had smeared his face black with ink. At the sight, Li Kui bellowed, “What damned creature are you to dare waylay travelers here?” The man said, “If you ask my name, it will frighten the heart out of you. Your lord and master is called the ‘Black Whirlwind.’ Leave your road money and your bundle, and I’ll spare your life and let you pass.” Li Kui roared with laughter. “What damned nonsense! Who the devil are you? Where did you come from? How dare you steal my name and run wild here?” Li Kui raised the broad-bladed sword in his hand and charged. The man could not withstand him and was just about to flee when Li Kui struck him in the thigh with the blade and knocked him to the ground. Planting a foot on his chest, Li Kui shouted, “Do you know who your lord and master is now?” From the ground the man cried, “Grandfather, spare your child’s life!” Li Kui said, “I am Li Kui, the famous hero of the rivers and lakes known as the ‘Black Whirlwind.’ You are the scoundrel who has disgraced my name!” The man said, “Though my surname is Li, I am not the true ‘Black Whirlwind.’ Your honored name is renowned throughout the rivers and lakes; at the mere mention of that mighty hero, even spirits and demons tremble. That is why I stole your name and took to waylaying travelers here. Whenever a lone traveler passed by and heard the words ‘Black Whirlwind,’ he would abandon his baggage and run. That is how I made these few gains; I truly never dared harm anyone. My own humble name is Li Gui, and I live in the village just ahead.” Li Kui said, “What an insolent rogue! You rob people of their bundles and baggage here, ruin my reputation, and even imitate me by wielding two broad axes. Let him first taste one blow from my axe!” He snatched an axe from the man’s hand and was about to strike. Li Gui cried out in panic, “Grandfather, if you kill me, you will be killing two people!” Hearing this, Li Kui stayed his hand and asked, “How does killing you amount to killing two people?” Li Gui said, “I never wished to become a highwayman, but at home I have a ninety-year-old mother with no one to support her. So I merely invoked your honored name to frighten people and took the bundles of lone travelers to provide for my old mother. In truth, I have never dared hurt a single person. If you kill me now, my old mother at home will surely starve to death.”

p.src: By the hour of the Snake, he was growing both hungry and thirsty. Mountain tracks and narrow paths surrounded him, and not a single wineshop or eating house was in sight. As he continued, he saw two thatched cottages peeping from a hollow in the distant hills. Li Kui hurried to the dwelling. A woman came out from the rear, her hair tied in a rough knot with a cluster of wildflowers at her temple, her face thickly painted with rouge and powder. Li Kui set down his broad-bladed sword and said, “Good sister, I am a traveler passing through. I am hungry and can find no wineshop or eating house. I’ll give you a full string of cash if you will kindly provide me with some wine and food.” Seeing Li Kui’s fearsome appearance, the woman dared not refuse and answered, “There is nowhere to buy wine, but I can cook you some rice before you go.” Li Kui said, “That will do. Just make plenty, for I am damned near starving.” The woman asked, “Would one sheng of rice be enough?” Li Kui said, “Cook three sheng of rice for me.” The woman lit a fire in the kitchen, then went to the stream to wash the rice and brought it back to cook. Li Kui went around behind the house toward the mountainside to relieve himself, and saw a man limping home from behind the hill. When Li Kui went behind the house to listen, the woman was just opening the back door to climb the hill for vegetables. Seeing the man, she asked, “Brother, where did you hurt your leg?” The man answered, “Wife, I very nearly never saw you again. Can you imagine my damned bad luck? I went out hoping to catch a lone traveler. I waited a full half month without making a single score, and today I finally happened upon one—and who do you think it was? It was none other than the real ‘Black Whirlwind.’ Damn my luck for running into that brute! How could I possibly stand against him? He struck me with his broad-bladed sword and knocked me to the ground, determined to kill me. So I pretended and cried, ‘If you kill me, you will have killed two people.’ He asked me why, and I told him, ‘At home I have a ninety-year-old mother with no one to support her. She will surely starve to death.’ The fool truly believed me. He spared my life and even gave me an ingot of silver as capital, telling me to change my trade and support my mother. I was afraid he might realize the truth and come chasing after me, so I slept for a while in a secluded place away from the grove, then returned home by way of the back hill.” The woman said, “Keep your voice down. A black-faced giant came to the house just now and told me to cook him rice. Could it be the very man? He is sitting out front now. Go and take a look. If it is he, go find some drug and put it in the vegetables. Once the scoundrel eats them, he will fall senseless. Then you and I can finish him off, seize whatever gold and silver he has, move into the county town, and start some business. Would that not be far better than waylaying travelers here?”

p.src: Li Kui heard every word and said, “Damn that scoundrel! I gave him a piece of silver and even spared his life, yet now he means to kill me. This is more than justice can abide.” He doubled back to the rear door. Just as Li Gui was about to leave, Li Kui seized him with one powerful hand, while the woman fled in panic through the front door. Li Kui caught Li Gui, threw him face-down on the ground, drew the knife at his waist, and promptly cut off his head. Knife in hand, he rushed out the front door in search of the woman, but she had vanished no one knew where. He went back inside and searched the rooms. He found two bamboo hampers containing some old clothes; beneath them he discovered some bits of silver and several hairpins and bracelets, all of which he took. He also searched Li Gui’s body and recovered the small ingot of silver, then tied everything into his bundle. When he looked in the pot, the three sheng of rice were already cooked, but there were no vegetables to eat with it. Li Kui served himself some rice and ate awhile. Looking about him, he laughed to himself and said, “What a fool I am! Here is good meat lying right before me, and I never thought to eat it.” Drawing his waist knife, he cut two pieces of flesh from Li Gui’s thigh, washed them clean with water, raked some coals from the stove, and roasted them. He ate as he roasted the meat. When he was full, he dragged Li Gui’s corpse beneath the house, set the place afire, took up his broad-bladed staff, and went off along the mountain road.

He went back inside and searched the rooms. He found two bamboo hampers containing some old clothes; beneath them he discovered some bits of silver and several hairpins and bracelets, all of which he took.
He also searched Li Gui’s body and recovered the small ingot of silver, then tied everything into his bundle.
When he looked in the pot, the three sheng of rice were already cooked, but there were no vegetables to eat with it.
Li Kui served himself some rice and ate awhile. Looking about him, he laughed to himself and said, “What a fool I am! Here is good meat lying right before me, and I never thought to eat it.”
Drawing his waist knife, he cut two pieces of flesh from Li Gui’s thigh, washed them clean with water, raked some coals from the stove, and roasted them.
He ate as he roasted the meat. When he was full, he dragged Li Gui’s corpse beneath the house, set the place afire, took up his broad-bladed staff, and went off along the mountain road.

I thought of you constantly and wept until my tears ran dry; that is why both my eyes went blind. Then he thought, “How can I carry some of this water back for Mother to drink?” He rose and looked east and west. Far away on a hilltop he spied a small hermitage and said, “Good!” Clinging to vines and creepers, he climbed to the hermitage and pushed open its door. It proved to be a shrine to the Great Sage of Sizhou. Before it stood a stone incense burner. Li Kui tried to lift it with his hands, but discovered that it had been carved in one piece with its pedestal. He tugged at it for a while, but could not pull it free. His temper suddenly flared. He wrenched out the pedestal with it, struck it against the stone steps in front, and knocked the incense burner off. Finding his former path again, he scrambled this way and that up the ridge.

p.src: Li Kui thought, “I came back from the Liangshan Marsh especially to fetch my old mother. After enduring untold hardships and carrying her all the way here, I have let you devour her! If the wretched tiger that dragged away this human leg did not take my mother’s, whose could it be?” Rage blazed in his heart, and his reddish-yellow whiskers bristled. Raising the broad-bladed sword in his hand, he thrust at the two cubs. The young tigers panicked under his thrusts, yet bared their fangs, brandished their claws, and sprang at him. Li Kui struck and stabbed one of them dead. The other darted into the cave. Li Kui pursued it inside and stabbed it dead as well. Li Kui then crawled into the tigers’ den and, crouching within, peered outside. Presently he saw the tigress approaching the lair, fangs bared and claws flailing. Li Kui said, “You are the accursed beast that ate my mother!” He laid down his broad-bladed sword and drew the short sword from his waist. On reaching the cave mouth, the tigress first swept her tail into the den, then backed the rear half of her body inside. Watching closely from within the den, Li Kui drove his blade beneath the tigress’s tail with all the strength of his life, heedless of death, and struck squarely into her anus. So mighty was Li Kui’s thrust that even the hilt went straight into her belly. The tigress roared and, with the blade still in her, leapt away from the cave mouth and across to the ravine. Li Kui seized his broad-bladed sword and rushed out of the cave in pursuit. Maddened by pain, the tiger plunged straight down beneath the rocky cliffs of the mountain. Just as Li Kui was about to pursue her, a sudden gale whirled up beside the trees, sending dead leaves and broken branches raining down. As the ancient saying goes, “Clouds arise with the dragon; winds arise with the tiger.” Where the wind arose, beneath the radiance of the stars and moon, a tremendous roar sounded, and suddenly a white-browed tiger with glaring eyes sprang forth. The tiger sprang ferociously at Li Kui. Unhurried and unafraid, he used the force of its own charge, swept up his blade, and struck it squarely beneath the jaw. The tiger could neither stretch nor pounce again: first because it recoiled from the pain, and second because its windpipe had been wounded. It had retreated scarcely five or seven paces when there came a crash like half a mountain collapsing, and in an instant it lay dead beneath the cliff.

p.src: Li Kui was now both hungry and thirsty. He had no choice but to gather his bundle, take up his broad-bladed sword, find the path, and walk slowly over the ridge. There he saw five or seven hunters gathering up their concealed bows, crossbows, and arrows. When they saw Li Kui, his whole body stained with blood, coming down the ridge, they were startled and asked, “Traveler, are you perhaps a mountain god or a local earth deity? How else would you dare cross the ridge alone?” At their question, Li Kui thought to himself, “Yishui County has now posted a proclamation offering three thousand strings of cash for my capture. How could I dare tell them the truth? I had better tell them a lie.” He answered, “I am merely a traveler. Last night I was crossing the ridge with my mother. When she asked for water, I went down below the ridge to fetch some, and a tiger dragged her away and ate her. I tracked it all the way to its den, killed two cubs first and then two grown tigers, slept in the temple of the Great Sage of Sizhou until dawn, and have only just come down.” The hunters cried out together, “We do not believe you! How could one man kill four tigers? Even Li Cunxiao and Zilu could each strike down only one. Those two cubs would be no great matter, but the two grown tigers were fearsome indeed. Because of those two beasts, we have endured no end of beatings. Ever since that family of tigers settled on Yi Ridge, no one has dared travel this road for a full three to five months. We do not believe you. Are you trying to fool us?” Li Kui said, “I am not even from these parts. Why would I deceive you for no reason? If you do not believe me, I will go back up the ridge with you and find them for you. Just bring some men along to carry them down.” The hunters said, “If it is truly so, we shall reward you handsomely. What splendid news that would be!”

p.src: The hunters raised their whistles, and within moments thirty or fifty men had gathered. Armed with hooks, spears, and staves, they followed Li Kui back up the ridge. By then it was broad daylight. When they reached the summit, they saw from afar that two tiger cubs had indeed been killed beside the den—one inside and one outside. A tigress lay dead by the rocky cliff, and a male tiger before the Temple of the Great Sage of Sizhou. Seeing all four tigers dead, the hunters rejoiced. They bound the carcasses with ropes and carried them down the ridge, inviting Li Kui to go with them and claim the reward. Meanwhile, they sent men ahead to inform the village headman and leading householders, who all came out to welcome them. The tigers were carried to the estate of a wealthy man known as Squire Cao. The man had once been a minor clerk and made a practice of bullying and extorting people in the countryside. Lately he had suddenly come into a few strings of spare cash, but his conduct remained mean and underhanded. Squire Cao came out in person to receive him, invited Li Kui into the reception hall, and, once they were seated, asked how he had killed the tigers. How are we to rescue him? Song Gongming was particularly concerned that some harm might befall him and sent me to learn what had happened. Now that he has been captured, if I fail to save him, how can I return to the stronghold and face our elder brother? What are we to do?” Zhu Fu said, “Brother, do not panic just yet. Constable Li is highly skilled; even thirty or fifty men cannot get near him. Though you and I may be of one heart and mind, how could the two of us dare approach him? We can only take him by cunning, not oppose him by force. Li Yun has always been very fond of me and often taught me how to wield various weapons. I do have a plan for dealing with him, but afterward I shall no longer be able to remain here. Tonight we shall cook twenty or thirty catties of meat and prepare more than ten jars of wine. We shall cut the meat into great chunks and mix knockout drug into it. At the fifth watch, we two will take several servants to carry it to a secluded spot halfway along the road and wait for them to escort him past. We shall pretend to offer wine in congratulations, drug everyone unconscious, and then release Li Kui. What do you say?” Zhu Gui said, “An excellent plan! There is no time to lose. Let us make everything ready and set out early.” Zhu Fu said, “But Li Yun cannot drink. Even if the drug fells him, he will awaken before long. And there is one more thing: if the truth comes out afterward, I shall certainly be unable to remain here.” Zhu Gui said, “Brother, there is little future in your selling wine here anyway. Then we shall all go up the mountain. I have a packet of knockout drug here in my bundle. Since Li Yun cannot drink, we shall sprinkle extra into the meat and press him to eat plenty.
